card.title: FIAT BR.20
card.text: Deployment: Add two 3rd ALPINI REGIMENT to your support line.
card.flavorText: The Fiat BR.20 “Cicogna” (Italian for Stork) was an Italian twin-engine medium bomber, developed by the Fiat aircraft company, and used by the Regia Aeronautica (Italian Royal Air Force) and other air forces. The Fiat BR.20 is the first all-metal Italian bomber.It entered service in 1936 and flew its first combat mission in 1937 when it was used in support of Franco’s Nationalist forces during the Spanish Civil War. The aircraft was also used by the Imperial Japanese Air Force during the Second Sino-Japanese war in 1937. In June 1940, Italy declared war on France and the UK, and it was used successfully during the short lived campaign against France. However, during The Battle of Britain the BR.20 showed its limitations for the first time. The harsh climate conditions over the channel made them vulnerable to mechanical failure, plus their defensive armaments were insufficient against the British fighters. The Fiat BR.20 also saw use in North Africa, where the desert environment also caused mechanical problems for the aircraft. The aircraft saw limited use in the Soviet Union, Malta, Albania and Greece, but the BR.20’s role in major operations diminished as the war progressed. This was both due to the shortcomings of the aircraft and because the Italian industry struggled to produce enough aircraft to meet the demand. However, some units continued to use the BR.20 throughout the war, but mainly for reconnaissance and transport missions. A total of 500 Fiat BR.20s were built, including a few variants. None of the aircraft remain today.
